misconceptions.description: Believing a revision log should record surface details (font, color, time spent) instead of what changed and why
misconceptions.trigger: learner logs cosmetic facts but not the reason or prompt for a change
misconceptions.feedback: Log what changed, why it changed, and what prompted it. Fonts and timestamps do not show your reasoning.

misconceptions.description: Writing log rows so vague ("fixed some stuff") that a reader cannot locate or understand the change
misconceptions.trigger: learner's log entry names no location, exact edit, or prompt
misconceptions.feedback: Name the location, the exact change, and the feedback or evidence that prompted it, so a reader can follow you.

misconceptions.description: Leaving AI-generated edits out of the log so the work looks fully self-produced
misconceptions.trigger: learner omits which edits came from a tool and which they accepted or rejected
misconceptions.feedback: Record AI's proposals and your accept or reject decisions. Hiding the tool hides your judgment, which is the point of the log.

misconceptions.description: Saving over the previous version each time instead of keeping a dated trail you can trace or roll back
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps only the latest file and cannot reconstruct earlier decisions
misconceptions.feedback: Keep a dated trail. It lets you trace the sequence of decisions and recover an earlier choice if a later one was worse.
